In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, while the participants generally used contextual information to infer unknown words, their use of morphological information depended on semantic consistency between morphological and context information.

Japanese EFL learners' lexical inferencing processes can be characterized as being flexible, depending on the semantic consistency of contextual and morphological clues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inferential process of Japanese EFL learners is flexible and contextually sensitive.
, in the process of lexical inferencing, participants used available information flexibly, and that their inferential processes were not limited to either morphological or contextual information.
, in inferring the meanings for unknown words, Japanese EFL learners flexibly use various inferential strategies, including literal interpretations of morphemes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learners are not always able to ignore contextual clues even when inferring literal meanings of words from their morphemes, and that they are not always able, or willing, to do so.
, in order to understand the processes involved in inferring the meanings, it is important that we take into account the various types of information that are available to language learners.
, in the case of opaque words, the meanings inferred from context are not always literal interpretations.
